Both K1 and K2 can act as
vitamin K-dependent
carboxylases.
Vitamin K serves as
a cofactor for the g-
glutamyl carboxylases
involved in activating
six clotting factors
involved in the control
of coagulation. In
addition, vitamin K is
also a cofactor for the
matrix Gla-proteins and
osteocalcin essential in
the regulation of matrix
and bone calciﬁcation.
As a cofactor for g-glutamyl
carboxylases, the
mechanism involves ﬁrst
the generation of a strong
base by oxygenation of
vitamin K. Vitamin K is
converted to vitamin K
epoxide, the intermediate of
which is a highly basic
alkoxide. This intermediate
is thought to abstract
hydrogen from targeted
glutamyl g-carbons to
facilitate CO2 addition to
form glutamyl residues.
